supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded creation of the non-temporary account it_support by raj.patel at 13:46:58 UTC.

One second later, the same subject and logon ID added it_support to the group named Administrators. This conflicts with the stated help-desk practice that temporary accounts are named tmp.<name> and added only to Temp-Staff.

Minutes before the account creation, raj.patel logged on to WS-TWEBER-01 via RDP from 203.0.113.17. The inventory says there is no VPN and remote administration is only done from WS-RPATEL-01, so this access is inconsistent with the stated practice.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs were not collected from 13:25 to 14:00 UTC, overlapping the alert window; proxy activity during that interval cannot be assessed.
The available records do not establish the source host or session that performed the account creation.
claims_not_established: Whether raj.patel authorized the account creation and administrator-group addition under an approved change.
Whether raj.patel's credentials or session were compromised.
Whether the account was subsequently used or what access it obtained.
Whether the RDP session from 203.0.113.17 directly caused the account creation.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm the account creation and group change against an approved change request and interview or verify with raj.patel through a trusted channel.
Review DC authentication and directory auditing to identify the originating host, logon session, and any subsequent activity by it_support.
Investigate the external RDP source and validate whether the session was authorized; preserve relevant endpoint and authentication evidence.
unrelated_findings: WS-TWEBER-01 recorded creation of a scheduled task named HealthCheck by raj.patel. Its hidden, encoded PowerShell action appears to retrieve and execute a script from http://203.0.113.17/a.ps1. The available evidence does not establish that this task is related to the alerted account creation; track it separately. (T097-00142)
